newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Dostum commander assassinated in north Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Dostum commander assassinated in north Afghanistan.

text.p: A senior Afghan commander in the northern Uzbek militia led by General Abdul Rashid Dostum was assassinated in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif, a party official said on Friday.
Mullah Abdur Rahman Haqqani, an ethnic Uzbek, was shot dead along with 10 bodyguards on Thursday, said Jandal Fateh Mohammed, an Islamabad-based spokesman for Dostum's Jumbish-i-Milli faction.
Haqqani, aged about 50, commanded 500 regular troops for Dostum, but could raise about 2,000 irregulars in time of need, the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) agency said.

AIP said Haqqani, from Keshendeh district in Balkh province, was a key Dostum commander, adding that his killing coincided with tension between Jumbish-i-Milli and the Jamiat-i-Islami faction led by former government commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
Ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani formed a new government last week in which Dostum's faction was allotted the defence ministry and other posts. No post was announced for Masood.
Masood formed a military alliance with Dostum, an old rival, and with a Shi'ite Moslem faction after the Islamic Taleban militia captured Kabul from the Rabbani government in September.
Haqqani, then a member of the Harakat-i-Inqilab-i-Islami faction, was involved in clashes with Jamiat supporters in the early 1980s when Soviet troops occupied Afghanistan, AIP said.
At least 100 people were killed in that feud, including a Jamiat commander named Zebihullah, who died in a mine explosion. Jamiat supporters blamed Haqqani for his death.
